confidence_notes: I based the food and drink anchors on three web searches. One got the RBA rate. Two checked prices from cost-of-living aggregators (Expatica/Numbeo data from June 2026, Numbeo, idealista, Citycost from October 2026, GoWira and Expatistan). Restaurant meals and cappuccino prices are the most reliable, because the sources mostly agree: about EUR 15.60-18 for a cheap meal, about EUR 70-71 for a mid-range meal for two, and about EUR 1.80-1.90 for a cappuccino. Beer is less certain. Numbeo-based data gives about EUR 6-6.25 for a 0.5 L pint, while idealista and GoWira say EUR 3.50-5. I used about EUR 5 for a standard restaurant draft, which in Italy is often 0.4 L. No Pisa-specific aggregate for wine by the glass was found, so I estimated about EUR 5 from beer prices and regional Tuscan norms. For cocktails, Expatistan's crowd-sourced figure is about EUR 6 (club price). Florence aperitivo benchmarks run EUR 5-9, so I used about EUR 8. I converted euros to US dollars at about 1.10, which comes from the two RBA cross rates, so this conversion is only approximate. The accommodation anchors are holistic model estimates for the July 2026 summer peak. I did not search for them or check any live listings. Pisa's hostel and budget-hotel supply is limited and prices are pushed up by day-trip tourism to the Leaning Tower, so these anchors have the widest uncertainty.
comparable_city_reasoning: Pisa is a mid-sized Tuscan university and tourist city. Its food and drink prices are close to the Italian average, with restaurants slightly cheaper than average, and below Florence and Milan (Citycost says living costs are about 11% below Milan). For accommodation in July, I compared it with Lucca and the smaller Florence-region markets during the summer peak.
